startingRequest: We want an AI agent that can automate customer service.
profile: A regulated financial-services company with 450 support specialists, centralized identity, mixed cloud and legacy systems, and strict audit requirements.

systems.name: Northstar SSO
systems.note: OIDC, employee groups, and step-up authentication

systems.name: Atlas CRM
systems.note: Customer profile data synchronized every 24 hours

systems.name: Polaris Knowledge
systems.note: Public, operations, manager, and compliance policies

systems.name: Ledger API
systems.note: Real-time balances and payment status behind an API gateway

scenarios.title: The vague request
scenarios.signal: Executives ask for an AI agent before establishing a support baseline.
scenarios.customerProblem: Slow resolution is a symptom; the actual workflow bottleneck and desired outcome are unknown.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: What must you learn before selecting a solution?

scenarios.title: Permission-sensitive knowledge
scenarios.signal: A specialist retrieves a manager-only refund exception during a demo.
scenarios.customerProblem: Naive retrieval discarded source permissions and created a regulated data leak.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: Where must identity and authorization be enforced?

scenarios.title: Correct model, stale data
scenarios.signal: The assistant returns yesterday's balance with high confidence.
scenarios.customerProblem: Atlas CRM synchronization is 24 hours behind the real-time Ledger API.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: Which source owns freshness for this answer?

scenarios.title: The risky refund
scenarios.signal: The agent attempts a high-value refund without review.
scenarios.customerProblem: Tool access exceeds the agent's safe autonomy boundary and lacks approval.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: Which actions require deterministic policy and human approval?

scenarios.title: The demo does not generalize
scenarios.signal: Production staff use abbreviations absent from formal policy documents.
scenarios.customerProblem: The curated demo hid a vocabulary mismatch and weak retrieval evaluation set.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: How will you isolate and measure retrieval quality?

scenarios.title: CRM rate limits
scenarios.signal: Peak support traffic causes cascading Atlas CRM failures.
scenarios.customerProblem: The synchronous integration has no caching, backoff, queue, or graceful fallback.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: How should the solution behave when the dependency is constrained?

scenarios.title: Users do not trust it
scenarios.signal: Answers are mostly correct, but weekly adoption remains below ten percent.
scenarios.customerProblem: The assistant lacks citations, workflow fit, and a credible feedback path.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: What evidence would make a specialist rely on the answer?

scenarios.title: Cost per task rises
scenarios.signal: Long contexts and expensive model routing make each resolution uneconomic.
scenarios.customerProblem: The architecture optimized demo quality without a unit-economics constraint.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: Which quality-preserving levers reduce cost per successful task?

scenarios.title: A downstream outage
scenarios.signal: Ledger API failure traps the agent in repeated tool calls.
scenarios.customerProblem: The agent lacks bounded retries, failure isolation, fallback, and escalation.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: How will the system stop safely and preserve user context?

scenarios.title: The executive ROI review
scenarios.signal: The CIO asks what business result the program actually created.
scenarios.customerProblem: The team tracked model accuracy but not adoption, cycle time, cost, or intervention rate.
scenarios.fieldQuestion: Which baseline and outcome metrics make impact defensible?
